mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i (1KR-FE) engine replacement typically costs £800-£1,200 for a rebuilt unit, £500-£800 for reconditioned, and £250-£500 for a used engine. Supply and fit adds approximately £400-£600 depending on the specialist and your location. Rebuilt engines include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty. Used engines are the cheapest option but carry higher risk. Always confirm warranty terms with your chosen supplier.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of head gasket failure in a Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include white smoke from the exhaust, coolant loss without visible leaks, overheating, milky oil (mayonnaise-like substance on the oil cap), and engine misfire. Head gasket failure on the 1KR-FE is one of the most common reasons for engine replacement in the Aygo 1.0 VVT-i. Head gasket replacement costs £450-£700 at specialist rates. Delaying repair can cause cylinder or piston damage. Regular coolant level checks can help catch the issue early.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 2005-2018 Aygo 1.0 VVT-i is valued between £1,000 and £5,000. With a rebuilt engine costing £800-£1,200, replacement is usually worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise in good condition. For vehicles worth under £2,000, a used engine may offer better value. Replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. Rebuilt engines come with a 12-month warranty for peace of mind. Always get a vehicle value check before committing to a full rebuild.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical engine replacement on a Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i takes 1-2 working days for supply and fit through a specialist. Used engines may be available faster if already in stock; rebuilt engines typically require longer lead times due to the reconditioning process. Most specialists offer next-day or 48-hour delivery on used units. Rebuilt engines typically require 3-5 working days. The 1KR-FE is a straightforward swap for most independent garages.

mainEntity.name: Is the Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i engine the same as the Peugeot 108 and Citroën C1?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The 1KR-FE engine in the Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i is identical to the engines fitted in the Peugeot 107/108 and Citroën C1. This means used engines from these vehicles are interchangeable, giving you more sourcing options. All three cars share the same 1KR-FE and 1KR-B52 engines. Engine mounts and ECU configurations are the same. Always verify the engine code before purchasing.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: All engines supplied through EnginesMarket carry a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with 30-90 days cover, while reconditioned and rebuilt units offer 12-month coverage. 12-month warranty covers parts and labour on rebuilt engines. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier. Warranty transfer options may be available depending on the supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i was launched in 2005 as Toyota's entry-level city car, developed alongside the Peugeot 107 and Citroën C1. Powered by the 1KR-FE 1.0-litre three-cylinder petrol engine, it became a UK bestseller among budget-conscious city car owners. The engine received a significant update in 2018 with the introduction of the 1KR-B52 variant to meet stricter Euro 6.2 emissions standards, with production continuing through the Aygo X crossover model.

milestones.description: First-generation Aygo (AB10) launched with 1KR-FE 1.0-litre three-cylinder petrol engine, 68 bhp (50 kW)
Second-generation Aygo (AB40) introduced; 1KR-FE engine carries over with minor refinements
1KR-FE replaced by 1KR-B52 (72 bhp) to meet Euro 6.2 emissions standards
Aygo X (AB70) launched, retaining the 1KR-B52 engine with updated calibration
Aygo X gains 1.5-litre hybrid option; 1KR-B52 remains available on base models

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i's 1KR-FE and 1KR-B52 engines are generally robust and reliable. However, certain failure points emerge at higher mileages - head gasket failure, water pump wear, and timing chain stretch are the most common reasons for replacement. Rebuilt Aygo 1.0 VVT-i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Head Gasket Failure - Why the Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i 1KR-FE Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The 1KR-FE engine can suffer head gasket failure due to overheating caused by cooling system leaks or water pump failure. The aluminium cylinder head and block expand at different rates, compromising the gasket seal.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace head gasket, skim head if warped, replace coolant
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before cylinder or piston damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best if gasket failure has caused cylinder or piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2005-2018 Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i is valued between £1,000 and £5,000 depending on condition, mileage and generation. For vehicles worth under £2,000, a used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. For vehicles worth £2,000-£5,000, reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. If the replacement cost approaches or exceeds the vehicle's value, evaluate scrap value first.
problems.recommendation: If you catch head gasket failure early (white smoke, coolant loss, overheating), the gasket replacement route offers significantly better value than a full engine swap. If the engine has overheated severely or the gasket has failed catastrophically, a rebuilt 1KR-FE with upgraded components is the sensible long-term choice.

problems.h4: Water Pump Failure - Why the Toyota Aygo 1.0 VVT-i 1KR-FE Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The water pump on early 1KR-FE engines has a known design flaw - a tin pulley and thin base plate with inadequate sealing. The pump can fail suddenly, leading to coolant loss, overheating, and potential head gasket failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, coolant flush, new drive belt
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; preventative maintenance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both components; address root cause and damage
repairOptions.longevity: Best if water pump failure has caused overheating and gasket damage
Best if overheating has caused significant engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - a typical Aygo 1.0 VVT-i sits in the £1,000-£5,000 bracket. Water pump replacement is usually cost-effective even on lower-value cars.
problems.recommendation: Water pump failure is one of the most common issues on early Aygo 1.0 VVT-i models. If diagnosed early (coolant loss, whining noise), water pump replacement is the right call. If the car has overheated and the head gasket has failed as a result, a combined repair or full rebuild may be necessary.
